title: Mammalian Chromosome Analysis and Sorting by Flow Cytometry
protocol: Ensure cells growing exponentially in sub-confluent culture in flasks are truly sub-confluent and contain an exponentially growing monolayer of cells.
Add 10 µg/ml Colcemid solution to the flasks to a final concentration between 0.01 µg/ml and 0.1 µg/ml.
Incubate cells with Colcemid under normal growth conditions for 3 to 15 hr.
Shake off mitotic cells 2 to 3 times by holding the flask horizontally and “slapping” the side against your other hand, causing the medium in the flask to rapidly slosh across the monolayer.
Repeat shaking of mitotic cells 2 to 3 times carefully without causing a loss of membrane integrity.
Pour off medium into a 50-ml centrifuge tube on ice for recovery of mitotic cells.
Centrifuge for a normal duration at a normal speed for the cell type, typically 5 to 7 min at 400 × g.
Completely discard the supernatant.
Proceed with the chosen method of chromosome isolation.
Use an intercalating dye PI to stabilize the chromosome structure.
This protocol is recommended for species with small numbers of chromosomes or highly variable DNA content.
For example, resolve the karyotype of cloned Chinese hamster cells using the single-color method.
Add 0.5 ml PI solution A to each tube containing cell pellets and resuspend the pellet.
Allow cells to swell for 10 min at room temperature in the dark.
Place 10 µl of swollen cell suspension on a glass microscope slide marked with a wax pencil or crayon.
Cover the sample with a coverslip.
Observe under a fluorescence microscope.
Add 0.25 ml PI solution B to the current suspension of 0.5 ml.
Incubate at room temperature in the dark for 3 min.
Rapidly draw up and expel the suspension 4 to 5 times using a 3-ml syringe with a 22-gauge needle.
Incubate the chromosome suspension at 37°C in a water bath for 30 min.
Filter the suspension through 35- to 60-µm mesh.
Store the isolated chromosomes for ≤3 weeks at 4°C until further analysis.
Prepare 0.5 mg/ml Hoechst 33342 stock solution in DPBS.
Add 12.3 μl of the Hoechst 33342 stock to 1 ml of PI solution A containing cells (final concentration 10 μM).
Draw parallel lines on a glass microscope slide where the coverslip will be placed using a wax pencil or crayon.
Gently add a drop or two of the cell solution onto the slide.
Carefully place a coverslip over the drop.
Observe under a fluorescence microscope using ultraviolet excitation.
Initially, all cells in the suspension should stain with Hoechst 33342 and appear blue (under ultraviolet excitation) and larger than cells that are not in a hypotonic solution.
As time passes, the cell membranes begin to break, thereby allowing propidium iodide (PI) to enter, changing the appearance of the chromosomes to red.
If the cells are red immediately and the chromosomes appear bunched inside the cells, the solution may be too hypotonic, and optimal swelling will not be reached.
Try again with a higher concentration of KCl in both the PI solutions in Basic Protocol 2.
Culture, incubate, and shake off mitotic cells as in Basic Protocol 1, steps 1 to 4.
Transfer 3 ml suspension containing mitotic cells into each 50-ml centrifuge tube.
Spin down the tubes for 8 min at 400 × g, 4°C.
Discard the supernatant and flick the bottom of each tube several times to dislodge the pellet in the remaining volume.
Add 1 ml freshly prepared IB01 (LMW) isolation buffer and flick several times to resuspend.
Incubate the suspension for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 0.1 ml of 2.5% Triton X-100 for every 1 ml of sample suspension.
Let stand for 10 min at room temperature.
Slowly force the suspension three times through a 22-gauge needle on a 3- to 5-ml syringe to disperse the metaphase chromosomes and avoid clumping.
Pool tubes if necessary.
Incubate the samples for 30 min at 37°C in a water bath.
Make a 1 mg/ml PI stock solution in distilled water.
Add 20 μl of PI stock solution to 1.0 ml of chromosomes (final concentration 20 μg/ml).
Stain for ≥3 hr at room temperature before analysis to establish equilibrium.
Make a 0.5 mg/ml Hoechst 33258 stock solution in distilled water.
Add 4 μl of Hoechst 33258 stock solution to 1.0 ml of chromosomes (final concentration 2 μg/ml).
Stain for ≥3 hr at room temperature before analysis to establish equilibrium.
Make a 0.5 mg/ml Chromomycin A3 solution in ethanol.
Add 40 μl of Chromomycin A3 solution to 1.0 ml of chromosomes (final concentration 20 μg/ml).
Stain for ≥3 hr at room temperature before analysis to establish equilibrium.
Follow Basic Protocol 1 with 10^6 to 10^7 mitotic cells per tube.
Add 5 ml room-temperature Ohnuki's hypotonic swelling buffer per tube.
Transfer the cells into 15-ml polypropylene centrifuge tubes and incubate at room temperature for 70 min.
Centrifuge 5 min at 100 × g at room temperature.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant and flick the tube to dislodge the pellet in the residual volume.
Add 1.0 ml freshly prepared cold IB02 (HMW) isolation buffer to each tube and mix gently.
Vortex each tube vigorously for 30 s.
Place the samples on ice for 10 min.
Combine 10 µl chromosome suspension and 0.2 µl of 1 mg/ml PI stock solution (final concentration 20 µg/ml).
Observe chromosomes under a fluorescence microscope to determine the degree of dispersion and clumping.
If needed, repeat vortexing of the main suspension for 10 s.
Maintain the sample on ice while rechecking dispersion.
Repeat the vortexing cycle as needed.
Store chromosomes unstained for ≤1 year at 4°C.
Stain chromosomes with Hoechst 33258 and Chromomycin A3 for ≥3 hr before analysis to establish equilibrium.
Make a 0.5 mg/ml Hoechst stock solution in distilled water.
Add 4.5 µl of the Hoechst stock to 1.0 ml of chromosomes (final concentration 2.25 µg/ml).
Prepare a 308 µg/ml Chromomycin A3 stock solution in McIlvaine's buffer, pH 7.
Dilute the Chromomycin A3 stock with 5 mM MgCl2 at a ratio of 1:1.
Add 150 µl of the diluted Chromomycin A3 to 1.0 ml of chromosomes (final concentration 20 µg/ml).
Use large-volume polyamine buffer (LVPB) as sheath fluid during sorting.
Check each sample for high molecular weight before long-term sorting experiments.
Place 75 µl of the chromosomal preparation into a 1.5-ml microcentrifuge tube.
Add 25 µl nuclear lysis buffer.
Add 2.5 µl of 20% SDS.
Wait several seconds and then check the viscosity of the sample by stirring the preparation and by drawing a small quantity into a pipet tip and then withdrawing the tip from the preparation.
Sort chromosomes from a human/hamster hybrid cell within 1 week of isolation.
Prepare a single-chromosomal suspension for flow cytometric analysis.
Identify individual chromosomes using flow cytometry.
Apply appropriate gating strategies to isolate the chromosomal population of interest.
Use DNA dyes such as Hoechst 33258 and Chromomycin A3 to label chromosomes.
Display flow karyograms of sorted chromosomes with univariate and bivariate plots.
Verify instrument performance using uniform fluorescent microspheres excited by the lasers on the instrument.
Use Spherotech Ultra microspheres or appropriate quality-control microspheres for alignment.
Optimize instrument alignment using submicron microspheres.
Ensure that alignment particles are suitable for ultraviolet lasers if using Hoechst 33258.
Consult a trained field service engineer for chromosome analysis optimization.
Use fluorescence to trigger the instrument instead of light scatter for small objects like chromosomes.
Treat chromosomes as submicron objects during analysis and sorting.
Ensure all chromosomes are visible on the plot and not below the threshold value.
Use the smallest nozzle size available for chromosome sorting on a cell sorter.
Apply high sheath pressure and drop drive frequency during chromosome sorting.
Use sheath buffer to hydrodynamically focus the sample stream through the instrument nozzle and laser beam for cell sorting.
Ensure the composition of sheath buffer matches that of the final chromosome sample buffer to maintain uniform pH during high-pressure sorting.
Maintain chromosomes at 4°C in collection tubes filled with a compatible buffer for post-sort processing.
Sort chromosomes directly into polypropylene collection tubes to minimize electrical charge accumulation and droplet spatter.
Collect sorted chromosomes for post-sort purity analysis.
Perform post-sort purity analysis to ensure typical sort purities exceed 95%.
